steps.description: Pre-filter counts.csv to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample (the smallest group size here is 1). Build a DESeqDataSet (design ~condition) from the raw counts, compute DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors internally (do not pre-normalize), and extract normalized counts for both samples. Compute a descriptive log2 fold change (treated / control, using the normalized counts, e.g. log2((normCount_treated+pseudocount)/(normCount_control+pseudocount))) for every filtered gene. Set an explicit reference level for the condition factor (control as reference) and name the contrast as condition: treated vs control. Output a table of gene, normalized counts (both samples), and descriptive log2FC, ranked by |log2FC|, with the design's lack of replication stated in the output.

plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE (no replicates) + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 1 treated vs 1 control liver sample from salmon gene-level counts, with no biological replication in either group. Per the knowledge service's flag (R-0003), a design with n=1 per group cannot estimate within-group dispersion, so no valid p-value can be produced from a standard DESeq2/edgeR/limma inferential test. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC (vst-blind PCA, sample distance) on the two samples; (2) pre-filters low-count genes; (3) computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors and reports normalized counts plus a purely descriptive log2 fold change (treated vs control) with NO p-value/adjusted-p-value and no shrinkage or multiple-testing step (both are explicitly dropped by the rule engine for this design); (4) ranks all tested genes by the descriptive log2FC and runs preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome, WikiPathways, and MSigDB GO-BP as follow-up collections available in the reference store, itself reported as descriptive/hypothesis-generating with no set-level inferential claim; (5) produces a report stating the no-replication limitation explicitly, the design that would support inference, and full reproducibility metadata. The count source is salmon but the profile does not establish whether length correction (tximport/scaledTPM) was applied — the model is fit on the gene counts as delivered, with no length offset, and this limitation is stated in the report rather than invented.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If any group holds one sample, do no inferential differential expression test. Without within-group replication no dispersion can be estimated, and a p-value from such a design has no inferential basis. Report normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes, state that the design has no replication, and name the design that supports inference.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.

The design supports no inferential test, thus the enrichment is descriptive: rank the genes by the descriptive log2 fold change, report the leading edge of each set, and report no set-level p-value as evidence.

If any group holds one sample, do no inferential differential expression test. Report normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes, state that the design has no replication, and name the design that supports inference.
